title: P-256 sigma rho: metered branchy corrections with a blinded prefix chain, register-resident forward block, 2^20-walk batches, flag-carry finishes, eight-copy loops, implicit previous key, windowed batch inversion and a one-instruction anchor cap test

claims.statement: For uniform full-size P-256 Q=[x]P, the cold classical algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed H1, M1/L-ori conditional fresh-exposure, H3 pricing and H-trail (average correction count per trail) premises. Total charged work is at most 2^126.868143 units at C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions/unit. The walk is the predecessor's (A=2^24, K=2^32, theta=2^-60, residual Markov factor 400000) with tau=0.4943041 and batches of 2^20 walks. The batched step keeps the inherited field rows and tests, both loops unrolled eight times, the previous point's key read from the point buffer instead of a lane-record copy, and six product finishes per step branching on the carry flag. This revision changes only the fixed path: the once-per-round batch inversion is a 4-bit window over the same exponent p-2 (253 squarings and 39 multiplies against 255 and 127), and the production period-cap test (CAP_PERIODS=2^60) becomes one tbnz instead of lsr+cbnz, one instruction fewer per anchor block step. Every conditional field correction is still a forward branch whose taken fix-up adds its exact extra instructions to a run-wide meter capped after every round at n*CORR+LAMBDA_CAP, CORR=22.468426 per step (dy carries pad 0 by L-ori sign symmetry, all other sites 2^-10). Each global round blinds every batch's prefix chain with one fresh uniform unit rho (charged), so a lane's count depends on its walk point and a uniform prefix only. The cap's abort probability uses only the algorithm's own coins: per-trail Azuma-Hoeffding over independent trail starts with the average premise H-trail, and Hoeffding over independent per-round blinding noise; DELTA_CORR<5.07e-14; the work bound holds regardless. The fixed path is charged at 656,962,450 instructions per 2^20-walk plain round: the inherited 656,973,461 less the 11,011 instructions that the windowed inversion removes (Callgrind Ir in the organizer image: base 41,098,871 and patched 41,087,860 at 2^16 walks; the base binary reproduces the inherited published count and MD5 exactly; plus the inherited 1,024-instruction allowance per round). Anchor rounds are charged 3*(2^20-1)+9 more than a plain round: the inherited 4*(2^20-1)+9 less the measured 2^20-1 from the one-instruction cap test (2^16-walk anchor round 64: base 41,361,018, patched 41,284,472, a 76,546 difference equal to 11,011+65,535, with equal meters). So C_COMMON=626.578386 and the step charge is 649.052307 against the inherited 649.078434 and the predecessor's 714.759990. All preprocessing, failures, restarts, table initialization, lookup, transfers, replay, verification and output are included. Peak memory is below 2^77 bytes, preprocessing at most 2^62.848071 units, nonuniform advice zero, and the conditional success margin at least 1e-6 above 0.39. Production probability and universal instruction bounds remain heuristic premises, not certifications. Measurements and finite experiments retain their original scope and attribution.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the revised full production cost ledger (including the correction charge, its meter slack and abort term) and order certificate, then run the inherited complete reduced-order procedure at tau=0.4943, the production value on its 0.0001 grid, retaining failures and replay checks. The two results have distinct scopes; neither establishes production mixing.
